title: zig build test-integration is unreliable on this host under full ~40-binary concurrency: statement_timeout cancellations produce non-deterministic, non-reproducible failures
summary: While running the Step 00a Green-Main Gate for WF02-batch-0-20260811, `zig build test-integration` (default concurrency, ~40 binaries) reported 30 failing test files (84/117 steps succeeded). Postgres server logs (docker logs r-co-db_test-1) showed dozens of 'canceling statement due to statement timeout' errors clustered every ~65 seconds during the run, correlating with the shared bpm_test_migrations_public advisory-lock acquire (tests/integration/helpers.zig's statement_timeout='60s' being exceeded under this host's concurrent load). A second full run with -j4 (build-step concurrency limit) reduced failures to 20/117 but did not eliminate them. Comparing the two runs' failing-file sets: 20 files failed in BOTH runs, 10 failed ONLY in run 1, 3 failed ONLY in run 2 -- a non-deterministic, non-overlapping pattern across two runs of byte-identical code, which is inconsistent with a deterministic code regression. Spot-verified 3 of the failing files (iss0076_secrets_table_test, env01_test via test-integration-env01-tt, gh512_t010_regression_test via test-integration-gh512) in standalone isolation: all 3 pass cleanly (6/6 build steps, all tests green) with zero code changes.

root_cause.details: The test-integration umbrella schedules ~40 independent Zig test binaries concurrently (Zig's build graph has no ordering edge between declared siblings by default). Every binary's TestHarness.init() acquires the same process-wide Postgres advisory lock (pg_advisory_lock(hashtext('bpm_test_migrations_public'))) to serialize migration-application, under a bracketed lock_timeout widened to 90s for the acquire itself, but a fixed statement_timeout='60s' still governs the DDL work done once the lock is held (tests/integration/helpers.zig line 304). On this host, the number of binaries queuing simultaneously is apparently large enough that some queued binaries' eventual DDL work exceeds 60s and gets cancelled by statement_timeout, producing a generic PgError.ServerError that Zig's test runner reports as a hard test failure rather than a distinguishable retry-safe condition. This is a documented, previously-partially-addressed class of issue (ISS-0107/ISS-0110/ISS-0151/ISS-0659 all touch the same lock/timeout interaction) but the fixes so far have not eliminated contention-driven failures on at least this host under full default concurrency.

prevention: Consider raising statement_timeout for the TestHarness's DDL/migration-application window (or making it configurable via env var) to accommodate higher concurrency hosts, following the same 'bracket a wider timeout around exactly the operation that needs it, restore after' pattern already used for lock_timeout in helpers.zig.
Consider whether the test-integration umbrella should have a configurable default -j cap (e.g. via build.zig reading an env var) rather than relying on every invoker to remember to pass -j manually.

Any future ORCH Step 00a Green-Main Gate check on this host should be aware that a single full-concurrency zig build test-integration run reporting failures is not sufficient evidence of a real regression -- cross-check failing files via a standalone/targeted re-run (a dedicated build step like test-integration-<name> or test-integration-gh512 exists for many files) before concluding main is red. This issue exists so that diagnosis doesn't have to be redone from scratch on every future batch's gate check.
